data.name: Safety_AutoDisabled_Format
data.value: Hooking was turned off for this game after repeated crashes shortly after injection ({0}). You can turn it back on; the consent dialog will be shown again.

data.name: Safety_Blocked_Toggle_Format
data.value: Hooking is disabled for this game: {0}

data.name: Safety_Consent_AgentUnavailable
data.value: The capture agent is not connected. Nothing was enabled.

data.name: Safety_Consent_AntiCheat
data.value: Anti-cheat systems may flag or ban accounts. FrameLedger refuses to inject where it detects an anti-cheat, and it cannot guarantee it knows every anti-cheat. If one appears after injection, capture stops within 30 seconds of it being detected.

data.name: Safety_Consent_Enable
data.value: Enable hooking

data.name: Safety_Consent_Hooked
data.value: If you enable hooking (Tier 1): the session records every frame's time, the native and displayed frame rates, the render and output resolutions, the upscaler and its quality mode, frame generation, ray tracing, and the hardware telemetry this machine provides.

data.name: Safety_Consent_Injected
data.value: What is injected, and why: FrameLedger.Overlay.dll is loaded into the game process to measure, from inside it, the real render resolution, the upscaler and its quality mode, whether frame generation is active and by how much, and whether ray tracing is in use. Measuring from outside the process cannot establish these accurately.

data.name: Safety_Consent_Intro
data.value: Hooking loads a FrameLedger library into this game's process. This dialog states what that means for this game. It recommends neither choice.

data.name: Safety_Consent_KeepOff
data.value: Keep hooking off

data.name: Safety_Consent_NotHooked
data.value: If you do not enable hooking (Tier 2): the session records its start, end and duration, and the hardware telemetry this machine provides. Every frame-derived value on that session reads N/A. This needs no injection and no elevation, and it is what every game gets until it is individually enabled here.

data.name: Safety_Consent_Phrase
data.value: I ACCEPT THE INJECTION RISK

data.name: Safety_Consent_Terms
data.value: You are responsible for the terms of service of the games you play.

data.name: Safety_Consent_Title_Format
data.value: Enable hooking for {0}?

data.name: Safety_Consent_TypeToConfirm_Format
data.value: To enable hooking for this game, type exactly: {0}

data.name: Safety_Consent_VersionMismatch
data.value: This app and the capture agent carry different versions of this consent text. Nothing was enabled. Restart both, then try again.

data.name: Safety_RecordWithoutMeasuring
data.value: Record this session without measuring it

data.name: Safety_Refused_CouldNotVerify
data.value: FrameLedger could not verify this game's files for anti-cheat, so hooking stays off. It will check again when the game's files or the detection rules change.

data.name: Safety_Refused_Named_Format
data.value: {0} was detected in this game ({1}). FrameLedger will not inject into it, and nothing overrides that.

data.name: Safety_Refused_MachineWide_Format
data.value: {0} is running on this PC ({1}): a driver or service, which may belong to another game or program rather than this one. While it runs, FrameLedger injects into no game, and nothing overrides that.

data.name: Safety_Refused_Unnamed
data.value: An anti-cheat or anti-tamper module was detected in this game. FrameLedger will not inject into it, and nothing overrides that.

data.name: Safety_HookingTurnedOff
data.value: Hooking has been turned off for this game; its page says what was found.

data.name: Safety_Unhooked_Format
data.value: Capture stopped: {0} was detected while the game was running, and FrameLedger unhooked.

data.name: Safety_Unhooked_MachineWide_Format
data.value: Capture stopped: {0} started on this PC while the game was running ({1}) — a driver or service, which may belong to another game or program — and FrameLedger unhooked. The game's next session is measured again once it is no longer running.

data.name: Safety_Unhooked_Unnamed_Format
data.value: Capture stopped while the game was running — {0} — and FrameLedger unhooked.

data.name: Safety_Refused_TargetUnreadable
data.value: The game is running, but Windows would not let FrameLedger open its process: it is protected by an anti-cheat driver, or it runs as administrator while FrameLedger does not. Nothing was injected and this run was not measured. FrameLedger will not work around another product's protection. If the game itself runs as administrator, the agent's admin mode in Settings lets FrameLedger open it; a protected process stays closed.

data.name: Safety_Exception_Title_Format
data.value: Make a user-mode exception for {0}?

data.name: Safety_Exception_Intro_Format
data.value: FrameLedger found {0} in this game ({1}) and turned its hooking off. This dialog asks whether to make an exception for this game only. It recommends neither choice.

data.name: Safety_Exception_Why_Format
data.value: The exception is offered because {0} runs entirely in user mode — no kernel driver, no service and no driver file in the game's folder.

data.name: Safety_Exception_Trial
data.value: The first two sessions you play hooked under the exception are a trial. If either one does not go well — it crashes, records no frames, does not end normally, is stopped for safety, or something new is found — the exception ends, and no exception can be made for this game again. Two good sessions do not prove that the anti-cheat did not notice.

data.name: Safety_Exception_Risk_Format
data.value: The risk is the same as before, and it is yours. {0} is anti-cheat. It may detect FrameLedger in the game and warn, block or permanently ban your account — possibly days later, and FrameLedger cannot know whether it did. Sessions that went well before are no promise about the next one, or about the next update of the anti-cheat.

data.name: Safety_Exception_Still_Format
data.value: Under the exception the guard still runs every check, and still refuses a kernel driver in the game's folder, any other anti-cheat, an anti-cheat driver or service on this machine, a scan it cannot finish, and a title it refuses by name. The exception covers {0} and nothing else.

data.name: Safety_Exception_Ends
data.value: After the trial, the exception ends by itself when something new is found, when a session under it crashes or is stopped for safety, when FrameLedger stops observing because another anti-cheat loaded, or when the game is updated; you may then make it again. Turning the option off in Settings suspends it. You can withdraw it at any time.

data.name: Safety_Exception_Next
data.value: Making the exception does not turn hooking on. You turn hooking on for this game afterwards, through the usual consent dialog.

data.name: Safety_Exception_Online
data.value: FrameLedger is intended for offline and single-player play. Do not use this exception with a game you play online or competitively unless you accept losing that account.

data.name: Safety_Exception_Accept
data.value: I accept the risk of a ban for this game

data.name: Safety_Exception_Grant
data.value: Make the exception

data.name: Safety_Exception_Cancel
data.value: Keep it blocked

data.name: Safety_AdminMode_Title
data.value: Run the capture agent as administrator?

data.name: Safety_AdminMode_Intro
data.value: The capture agent normally runs with your standard rights, and every capture tier works that way. This option asks Windows to start it as administrator instead.

data.name: Safety_AdminMode_Adds
data.value: What it adds: FrameLedger can open and measure a game that itself runs as administrator, and it can read the CPU temperature where PawnIO is installed.

data.name: Safety_AdminMode_Unchanged
data.value: What it does not change: a game with anti-cheat is still refused, and a process Windows protects stays unreadable. A Vulkan game that runs as administrator is still not measured, because Windows does not load FrameLedger's Vulkan layer into it. Games you start from FrameLedger still run with your standard rights.

data.name: Safety_AdminMode_Prompt
data.value: Windows asks you every time the agent starts — at logon too, when its prompt may wait on the taskbar — and it names an unknown publisher, because FrameLedger is not signed. If you answer No, the agent runs with your standard rights and says so. If another administrator account answers, that agent refuses to run, because its data would not be yours.

data.name: Safety_AdminMode_Risk
data.value: The risk is yours: FrameLedger is installed in your user folder, which any program running under your account can change. A program that replaced FrameLedger's files would run as administrator the next time you accept this prompt. Turn this on only if you trust everything that runs under your account.

data.name: Safety_AdminMode_Accept
data.value: I understand, and I want Windows to ask each time the agent starts

data.name: Safety_AdminMode_TurnOn
data.value: Turn on

data.name: Safety_AdminMode_Cancel
data.value: Keep standard rights

data.name: Safety_Exception_VersionMismatch
data.value: This app and the capture agent carry different versions of this text. Nothing was granted. Restart both, then try again.

data.name: Safety_Exception_OptionOff
data.value: The user-mode exception option is off in Settings, so nothing was granted.
